name: bike-rebalance-two-truck-assignment
instruction:
# Assign and order two truck routes

Two trucks must collectively service every station in `/root/work/data.json` exactly once. Decide which truck visits each station and the order of visits. Both trucks must visit at least one station and return to the common depot.

The input gives `depot` coordinates, `vehicle_capacity`, and `vehicles`, an array of two objects with `vehicle_id` and `start_load`. Each station has a nonconsecutive integer `id`, coordinates, `initial_bikes`, `station_capacity`, and a signed `net_rebalancing_target`. At its visit, perform that target in full: a positive value picks bikes up from the station and increases truck load; a negative value drops bikes off and decreases load. Truck loads, including their initial and final loads, must lie between zero and `vehicle_capacity`. After service, each station's inventory must lie between zero and `station_capacity`.

Minimize the sum of both depot-to-depot travel distances. Use great-circle miles and Earth radius 3960.0, without rounding legs. Write `/root/work/assignment.json` containing exactly `vehicles` and `travel_distance_miles`. `vehicles` is in input vehicle order; each object contains exactly `vehicle_id`, `route`, `loads_after_stops`, and `end_load`. Routes use `"depot_start"`, station IDs, then `"depot_end"`. Loads are integer bike counts; round distance to six decimals. If distances tie within 1e-9 miles, select the lexicographically smallest pair of station-ID sequences in vehicle order.
